;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Syria missile strikes (September 2018)]]
**[[Russia]] and [[Turkey]] announce a [[demilitarized zone]] in [[Syria|Syria's]] [[Idlib Governorate]] and rule out any military operations. [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/middle-east/syria-war-idlib-russia-turkey-military-buffer-zone-government-rebel-violence-a8541946.html (''The Independent'')]
**[[Syria missile strikes (September 2018)|Several missiles are launched]] from the sea at the coastal city of [[Latakia]], some of which are destroyed by [[air defence]] systems. It is not immediately clear who was behind the attack. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-mideast-crisis-syria-attack/syrian-air-defences-down-missiles-fired-at-city-of-latakia-state-media-idUKKCN1LX2BS (Reuters)]
**A [[Russian Air Force]] [[Ilyushin Il-18|Ilyushin Il-20]] reconnaissance plane with 14 servicemen on board disappears from radar over the [[Mediterranean Sea]] during the missile attack on Syria's [[Latakia Governorate]]. A [[United States|U.S.]] official claims the [[Syrian Army]] inadvertently shot it down while attempting to intercept missiles, while Russia detected a missile launch from a French [[FREMM multipurpose frigate]]. [https://edition.cnn.com/2018/09/17/politics/syrian-regime-shoots-down-russian-plane/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-mideast-crisis-syria-russia/russia-says-a-military-aircraft-vanishes-near-syria-during-israeli-french-strikes-idUSKCN1LY057 (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-45556290 (BBC)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**The [[Taliban]] launches multiple attacks on security checkpoints in [[Afghanistan]], killing at least 27 members of the security forces. Twenty-two Taliban members are also killed and 16 others are injured. [https://www.news.com.au/world/breaking-news/taliban-kills-27-afghan-police-soldiers/news-story/fd07a6ad3de216f6d4d4e753c807cd7e (news.com.au)]
*Ethnic violence in [[Ethiopia]] over the weekend results in 23 deaths. Thousands protest against the killings in the capital [[Addis Ababa]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-violence/at-least-23-die-in-weekend-of-ethiopia-ethnic-violence-idUSKCN1LX0VK (Reuters)] [https://punchng.com/breaking-23-dead-in-ethiopia-ethnic-violence/ (''The Punch'')]

;Arts and culture
*[[70th Primetime Emmy Awards]]
**''[[The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel]]'' wins [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy series]] and ''[[Game of Thrones]]'' wins [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Drama Series|Outstanding Drama series]]. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/life/tv/2018/09/17/emmys-2018-live-tv-awards-hosted-michael-che-colin-jost/1339864002/ (''USA Today'')]

;Business and economy
*[[2018 China–United States trade war]]
**The [[United States]] announces a 10% [[tariff]] on $200 billion worth of Chinese goods to start on September 24, increasing to 25% by the end of the year, and threatens tariffs on an additional $267 billion worth of imports if [[China]] retaliates. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-trade-china-tariffs/trump-slaps-tariffs-on-200-billion-in-chinese-goods-threatens-267-billion-more-idUSKCN1LX2M3 (Reuters)]
*[[Phase-out of lightweight plastic bags]]
**The [[Cabinet of Jamaica|Jamaican Cabinet]] announces a total ban on the importation, manufacture, distribution and use of single-use plastic bags, effective January 1, 2019. [http://www.jamaicaobserver.com/latestnews/Gov%26%238217;t_ban_on_single_use_plastic_bags,_straws,_Styrofoam_starts_January (''Jamaica Observer'')]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Hurricane Florence]]
**The death toll rises to at least 32, as flooding continues to inundate [[North Carolina]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-45544424 (BBC)]
*[[2018 Pacific typhoon season]], [[Typhoon Mangkhut#Philippines|Typhoon Mangkhut]]
**In the [[Philippines]], [[Typhoon Mangkhut]] triggers a landslide in [[Itogon, Benguet|Itogon]], [[Benguet]], with more than 40 bodies found. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/typhoon-hit-philippines-rescuers-use-bare-hands-look-survivors-massive-n910111 (NBC News)] [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/17/world/asia/typhoon-mangkhut-philippines-china.html (''The New York Times'')]
**[[President of the Philippines|Philippine President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] repeats his call to shut all mines in the country following deadly landslides, hours after [[Secretary of Environment and Natural Resources (Philippines)|Environment and Natural Resources Secretary]] [[Roy Cimatu]] orders all mining to be stopped in the [[Cordillera Administrative Region|Cordillera region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-asia-storm-philippines-duterte/philippine-leader-again-vows-to-shut-mines-after-deadly-landslides-idUSKCN1LX15K (Reuters)]
*Over 100 people are killed in floods after [[Nigeria]]'s two major rivers burst their banks. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-45546695 (BBC)]
*At least 11 people were killed and several others injured in a road crash involving a bus travelling from [[Zambia]] to [[South Africa]]. [https://www.nation.co.ke/news/africa/South-Africa-road-crash-claims-11/1066-4764476-113ng9k/index.html (''Daily Nation'')]
*Seven people are killed and many others are in critical condition after suspected drug overdoses at a music festival in [[Hanoi]], [[Vietnam]]. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/seven-die-of-suspected-overdose-at-hanoi-music-fest-3810214.html (VnExpress International)]
*Five people are killed in a stampede at a [[Association football|football]] match in [[Luanda]], [[Angola]]. [https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2796121-5-people-killed-after-a-stampede-in-african-champions-league-match-in-angola (Bleacher Report)]

;Law and crime
*[[Disappearance of Sherlyn Cadapan and Karen Empeño]]
**Former [[Philippine Army]] general and politician [[Jovito Palparan]] is convicted for the kidnapping and disappearance of students Sherlyn Cadapan and Karen Empeño. He and two other associates are sentenced to [[life imprisonment]]. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/212145-bulacan-court-judgment-kidnapping-illegal-detention-cases-vs-jovito-palparan-september-17-2018 (''Rappler'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[Guatemala]]n [[President of Guatemala|President]] [[Jimmy Morales]], along with [[Ministry of the Interior (Guatemala)|Interior Minister]] Enrique Degenhart, [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Guatemala)|Foreign Minister]] [[Sandra Jovel]], and State Attorney Luis Donado say that they will not abide by the [[Constitutional Court of Guatemala|Constitutional Court]]'s resolution in which ordered President Morales and his cabinet to allow [[Iván Velásquez Gómez]], the head of the [[International Commission against Impunity in Guatemala]], to enter Guatemala. [https://www.nytimes.com/2018/09/17/world/americas/guatemala-democracy-under-threat.html (''The New York Times'')]

;Science and technology
*[[Exploration of Jupiter]]
**[[JunoCam]] captures an image of [[Jupiter]]'s "brown barge", a cyclone-like shape that has weather patterns in [[Atmosphere of Jupiter|Jupiter's atmosphere]]. [https://www.upi.com/Science_News/2018/09/17/Juno-image-showcases-Jupiters-brown-barge/4651537188944/ (UPI)]
*[[SpaceX lunar tourism mission]]
**[[SpaceX]] announces that [[Japan]]ese billionaire and art collector [[Yusaku Maezawa]] will be the first commercial passenger to orbit the [[Moon]] on their [[BFR (rocket)|BFR]] rocket in [[2023]]. [https://news.sky.com/story/japanese-billionaire-yusaku-maezawa-to-become-moon-space-tourist-11501082 (Sky News)]
*The world's first commercial [[Hydrail|hydrogen-powered passenger train]] enters service in [[Lower Saxony]], [[Germany]]. The [[Alstom]] developed train uses a [[hydrogen fuel cell]] which emits no [[carbon dioxide]]. [https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/en/news/20180917_04/ (NHK)]
